note: The collision half of 008. These bytes are a different file from 008's -- 0x80 rather than 0xFF, and 0xC3 is a third -- and all three decode to the same U+FFFD in Node, canonicalise to the same bytes, and produce the SAME receipt_sha256. A canonical form exists so that distinct documents have distinct bytes; canonical.py says so in as many words about allow_nan ('permitting them would let two different receipts share a canonical form'). Silent U+FFFD substitution breaks that property for every receipt reader built on Node or on the browser's TextDecoder, and it breaks it before any verifier code runs. The fix is to decode strictly -- Buffer/TextDecoder both offer a fatal mode -- and refuse, matching Python and Rust, which reports 'cannot read: stream did not contain valid UTF-8' and exits non-zero.
